title: Error Handling
summary: How Luau fails: error() raises, pcall/xpcall catch without killing the thread, assert() guards assumptions. Roblox scripts that error stop at the error line.

methods.name: error
methods.description: Raises an error, stopping the current thread unless caught. message can be any value (strings are friendliest for readers).

methods.name: pcall
methods.description: Protected call: runs f in protected mode. Returns true + results, or false + error message. Never throws.

methods.name: xpcall
methods.description: Like pcall, but passes errors through handler (commonly debug.traceback) for richer messages.

methods.name: assert
methods.description: Errors with message if v is falsy; otherwise returns v — usable inline: `local part = assert(workspace:FindFirstChild("Spawn"))`.

details.heading: Roblox specifics
details.body: An uncaught error in a Script/LocalScript halts that script at the offending line (the rest of the script doesn't run). Event callback errors don't disconnect the connection but abort that callback invocation. Errors print to the Output window with a stack trace.

explanation.whatItIs: The set of tools for saying 'this cannot continue' (error/assert) and for surviving other code saying it (pcall/xpcall).
explanation.whyItExists: Games hit the unexpected constantly: missing objects, bad remote arguments, flaky HTTP. Structured failure beats silent wrongness.
whenToUse: pcall around anything external: DataStore calls, HttpService, MarketplaceService
error() for programmer mistakes: bad arguments to your own functions
Retries: wrap pcall in a loop with backoff for service calls
whenNotToUse: Don't pcall-and-ignore errors blindly — at least log them
Don't use error() for normal control flow (use return values)
Don't wrap your entire script in one giant pcall — narrow the scope to the risky call
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
local ok, err = pcall(function()
    risky()
end)

if not ok then
    warn("risky failed:", err)   -- you survive
end
```
pcall is a safety net: whatever falls into it comes out as a value instead of crashing you.
tips: The canonical retry pattern for DataStores is pcall + loop (see the datastore pattern)
xpcall with debug.traceback gives you the call stack in the message
Studio's Output window is where all of this reports — keep it open while testing
commonMistakes: `local success, err = pcall(risky())` — that calls risky NOW; pass the function: `pcall(risky)`
Continuing as if success were true after pcall returned false
Raising errors with tables/objects as messages — unprintable in Output

examples.title: pcall + retry (the DataStore idiom)
examples.code:
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("PlayerData")

local function loadWithRetry(key, attempts)
    for i = 1, attempts do
        local ok, result = pcall(function()
            return store:GetAsync(key)
        end)
        if ok then
            return result
        end
        warn(`Attempt {i} failed: {result}`)
        task.wait(1)
    end
    error(`Failed to load {key} after {attempts} attempts`)
end

examples.title: assert for invariants
examples.code:
local function setupRound()
    local arena = assert(workspace:FindFirstChild("Arena"), "Arena missing from workspace!")
    local spawns = assert(arena:FindFirstChild("Spawns"), "No Spawns folder in Arena")
    print("Round ready:", #spawns:GetChildren(), "spawns")
end
examples.whyItWorks: assert either hands you the found instance or halts with a clear message — no nil-chasing later.
